facts.fact: Phase nine is functionally related to phase seven — the snap ring check performed in phase seven is repeated here in phase nine to confirm the snap ring is seated correctly.

citation.transcript_quote: we always used that before we actually use it in phase nine to make sure the snap ring is on correctly

facts.fact: The primary acceptance criterion for this check is that the ring retainer is fully seated all the way down — not a specific numeric Mitutoyo value.

citation.transcript_quote: All we are ensuring on this is making sure that it's all the way down

facts.fact: The operator does not verify a specific numeric target value from the Mitutoyo tool; they simply hit 'record' or 'next' to log the measurement and proceed.

citation.transcript_quote: We don't know the correct values, what it has to be at. All we do is hit record or next

facts.fact: After confirming the ring retainer is seated, spin the assembly by hand to verify it rotates easily without resistance ('spins easy, doesn't fight') as a secondary confirmation of correct assembly.
This ring retainer check can alternatively be performed during the phase seven step — it does not have to wait until phase nine.

citation.transcript_quote: You can do it in this step as well. Doesn't matter.
